summary: Without a subplan you show second-year proficiency in Chinese, Japanese or Korean; a subplan instead asks for third-year proficiency and adds its own courses. Everyone takes three area courses (humanities, history, social sciences), four thematically coherent East Asia courses with one numbered 200 or above (moved in by hand), a WIM course, and the Senior Colloquium (EALC 198) with a Senior Research course and a capstone essay, project or honors thesis. Courses outside the language requirement must be letter graded and at least 3 units. The major needs 78 units: other courses in the eligible subjects count toward them, at most 30 units of language courses count, and courses from other related departments are moved in by hand with the DUS's approval. You check by hand the 2.0 GPA, that each non-language course is taught by a faculty member with an EALC appointment, the subplans' approved content courses, and proficiency shown by exam; honors adds a 3.5 GPA, an approved proposal, an advanced seminar and the thesis. With the China, Japan or Korea subplan the WIM course must be CHINA 111, JAPAN 138 or KOREA 120 respectively; the East Asian Languages subplan's additional courses can come from any one of its four categories.

Demonstrate proficiency in Chinese, Japanese, or Korean language at the second-year level or above, to be met either by coursework or examination." The format cannot drop a rule when a subplan is chosen, so the third-year courses every subplan requires also meet it ("or above"), and it shares them. Proficiency by examination is marked done by hand. It applies only without a subplan (block nKhTrBNR is unlessSubplan), so it no longer shares its course with a subplan's language rule.

Fulfill ANY of the following requirements: Additional East Asian Language Proficiency OR Advanced Courses OR Classical East Asian Language Courses OR East Asian Cultural Content Courses." Any one of the four categories meets the rule; the rest of the 78 units come from further eligible courses. The two categories with no course list (another East Asian language, fourth-year or conversational courses) are approved and moved in by hand.
